basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment, cleft palate (3/5) and clubfeet (30-79%) characterize the syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia is 2/7; cardiac frequency is unclear.
Anatomic malformation of the thyroid, an endocrine gland.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 80-99% and causes respiratory failure.
Motor peripheral nerve disorder; the supplied concept does not establish an autoimmune mechanism.
Radiation directly injures marrow, skin and intestinal epithelium; dermal atrophy 80-99%, cytopenias 30-79%; neurologic and pulmonary injury are dose-dependent minorities.
Congenital microcephaly and intellectual disability occur in all 10 reported patients.
Ossification affects a spinal ligament; cord and root injury occur in symptomatic cases, but involvement in at least 30% across all patients is not established.
Brain malformations, coloboma/microphthalmia and hydronephrosis each 30-79%; cap omits oral malformations and microtia, also annotated 30-79%.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; developmental impairment and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy each 1/1 reported patient; respiratory insufficiency lacks evidence of direct lung disease.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; developmental delay 10/10. Extra-neural abnormalities are single-patient annotations without established population frequency.
Lysosomal storage with defining cognitive decline; skeletal/joint disease >80% and cardiac valve disease >50%; cap omits common airway and hearing impairment.
Inherited alpha-globin abnormality causes methemoglobinemia and impaired blood oxygen carriage; cyanosis does not establish lung injury.
Cerebellar and cerebral degeneration cause tremor, ataxia and other neurologic deficits.
Benign neoplasm arising from cutaneous sweat glands.
Defining intellectual disability and movement disorder; muscular dystrophy/myopathy and cataracts each occur in 30-79%; pulmonary and cardiac findings are under 30%.
Trichosporon fungal infection; superficial and disseminated forms affect different sites, with no additional organ established as common across the umbrella.
Retrograde movement of duodenal contents into the stomach; bile in reflux does not indicate hepatobiliary disease.
Cleft palate, eyelid blepharophimosis and male urethral hypospadias are defining malformations; intellectual disability occurs in under 30%.
PRPF31-associated retinal degeneration causes progressive visual impairment.
Arthrogryposis, neurodevelopmental impairment and orofacial cleft define syndrome; strabismus 80-99%; cap omits hearing abnormality (30-79%).
Testicular failure includes low testosterone in 1/3 and elevated LH in 2/3; endocrine classification is borderline because only three patients were reported.
Respiratory motile-cilium dysfunction impairs airway clearance; recurrent infections reflect the airway defect rather than primary immune disease.
Sensorineural deafness and missing teeth define the syndrome and each occur in 80-99%; vestibular symptoms remain within the otologic axis.
TAF4B-related spermatogenic failure affects reproduction; elevated FSH alone does not establish impaired gonadal hormone production.
Autoimmune autonomic ganglion injury; gastrointestinal dysmotility (~70-80%) and bladder dysfunction (~50%) cause functional loss; orthostatic hypotension alone is not vascular damage.
